1.content: When rating any move, first check if the resulting cell is a hazard; if so, assign a very large penalty so it will never be top‑rated. If the resulting cell is orthogonally adjacent to a hazard, assign a penalty that outweighs moderate progress bonuses, but if *all* safe moves provide zero or negative Manhattan distance reduction (i.e., no progress), allow a reduced adjacent‑hazard penalty so that a distance‑reducing move adjacent to a hazard can be rated higher than staying still or looping.

2.content: When rating a move, compute the Manhattan distance from the resulting cell to the goal. Apply a moderate positive bonus proportional to distance reduction, and apply a moderate penalty proportional to distance increase; moves that keep distance unchanged receive no bonus or penalty. This progress bonus should be added after any safety penalties, ensuring safe moves that also advance toward the goal are rated highest.
